contexts.text: Moles and bats () = those who are in darkness, that is, in falsities, and consequently in evils.
To bow themselves to the moles and to the bats () is to worship such things as are in thick darkness and in the shade of night, which is to worship outward things without anything inward.
Those who are there, and those who are like them, are called owls and bats. TCR 162:3.
They themselves are seen before the eyes of angelic Spirits, some as bats, some as owls. TCR 162:5.
They who are in falsified truths and adulterated goods appear as owls and bats.

In the cloud screech-owls and bats were flying about; and I was told, that the screech-owls and bats flying in the dusky cloud were correspondences, and consequently appearances of their thoughts; for confirmations of falsities so utter that they appear to be truths, are represented in that World under the forms of birds of night. TCR 334:8.
He sees no more than a bat in daylight.
At first he sees truths no otherwise than as a bat sees clothes hanging up in a garden, to which it flies as a refuge.
The evils and falsities of doctrine from which is their worship, are signified by the moles and the bats (), because their sight is in darkness, and they shun the light. AE 587:10.
